subject: Re: Private deployment — ephemeral tenant keys & offline escrow procedure
body:
From: Aurora Velasquez <aurora.velasquez@solacehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18 09:15 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: key rotation cadence & offsite escrow for audit

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are moving forward on the private deployment PoC in our AWS VPC but have a couple of security questions before the next milestone:

1) We need to ensure our long-term data encryption keys (DEKs) are under our control — ideally generated and wrapped by our on-prem HSM (YubiHSM/GCP CloudHSM equivalent). Can Redwood support a BYOK flow that never sends unwrapped DEKs outside our environment?

2) Audit requirement: for a scheduled audit (annual), we must provide a time-stamped, signed snapshot showing key rotation events and operator handoff logs. We cannot provide direct access to our HSM. Is there an accepted "offline escrow" format Redwood can produce that satisfies auditors?

3) Network constraint: our VPC is egress-restricted (no public outbound except specific endpoints). We need a plan that avoids opening broad internet access for key material flow.

Can you outline an approach and rough timeline? We prefer short, clear answers we can show our InfoSec team.

Thanks,
Aurora
Director, Infrastructure Security
Solace Health

-----Original Message-----

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Aurora Velasquez <aurora.velasquez@solacehealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-18 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: key rotation cadence & offsite escrow for audit

Aurora — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then a recommended pattern we can scope into the PoC: 

Short answers:
- BYOK: Yes. We can support a BYOK workflow where the customer-generated KEK (Key Encryption Key) never leaves the customer boundary unwrapped. Redwood accepts only wrapped keys and/or wrapped key-encryption-material.
- Offline escrow/audit: Yes. Redwood can produce signed, time-stamped key event bundles (CBOR/JSON) and an encrypted escrow package you can ingest into your evidence store. We will include operator signatures and an inclusion hash for each event.
- Network: For egress-restricted VPCs we use a local agent pattern (private deploy "kms-agent") that runs inside your VPC to perform wrapping/unwrapping operations without outbound access to public internet; Redwood communicates with the agent over private peering / cross-account VPC endpoints.

Recommended PoC pattern (concise):
1) Customer generates a KEK in their HSM (BYOK). Customer exports only a wrapped KEK blob using an agreed wrapping key (customer HSM local key). Redwood never receives unwrapped KEK.
2) Deploy a small, signed Redwood kms-agent in the customer VPC (single EC2/ECS task). The agent has no key material — it proxies HSM wrap/unwarp requests to the HSM over the private network.
3) Redwood runtime holds ephemeral tenant data keys (DEKs) in process memory and always stores them encrypted (wrapped) with the customer KEK. Key rotation is performed by generating new DEKs and re-wrapping under current KEK; KEK rotation triggers a re-wrap step during a controlled maintenance window.
4) Escrow: For audit, the kms-agent can export an encrypted, time-stamped bundle containing signed event logs (rotation, operator authorization, wrap/unwrap ops). Redwood adds its server-side signature to the bundle; the final artifact is encrypted with a customer-provided public key and delivered via S3 endpoint or an SFTP drop that meets your egress rules.

Next steps: aditya, laura, jonas — can we propose a 2-week PoC plan and a 1-hour discovery with Aurora's infra team to validate the agent+HSM connectivity?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Manager, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment: key rotation cadence & offline escrow for audit

Aurora — quick commercial note and an example artifact we can produce for audits.

Commercially, we typically include the kms-agent as part of the Private deployment package (no extra runtime charges for the agent itself). For escrow evidence delivery we can support either:
- S3 PUT into a customer-controlled bucket (we only get envelope-encrypted artifacts and never hold the unencrypted escrow), or
- Secure SFTP push to an endpoint you own; we will only push an encrypted zip with PGP+timestamp signature.

Attached: redwood-escrow-procedure-draft.pdf (draft format for the runbook and what auditors expect). If the auditors have a specific schema we can map fields to their required CSV/JSON manifest.

Proposed PoC timeline:
- Week 0: Discovery + network/agent footprint validation
- Week 1: Agent deploy + validate HSM wrapping (test vectors)
- Week 2: Rotation test + generate escrow artifact and validate ingestion to customer bucket

If that timeline works we can get a Statement of Work drafted.

—Aditya
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Aurora Velasquez <aurora.velasquez@solacehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-24 16:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: key rotation cadence & offline escrow for audit

Aurora — attaching a compact technical checklist and acceptance criteria below. I spoke with the infra team and verified the agent pattern is compatible with your egress rules (we'll use VPC endpoints + customer-controlled S3 or SFTP).

Acceptance checklist (items we will demo for your auditors):
1) BYOK enforcement: demo that KEK material cannot be exported unwrapped. Test vector: create KEK in customer HSM, produce a wrapped KEK blob; attempt to open wrapped blob without HSM -> should fail.
2) Rotation proof: show rotation event bundle (signed with Redwood operator key + agent signature) that includes a monotonic event id, timestamp, and operation type. Example fields: event_id, key_id (opaque), operation, operator, nonce, sig_redwood, sig_agent, audit_hash.
3) Escrow delivery: show encrypted escrow package stored in customer S3 (access logs and S3 versioning enabled) and verify customer can decrypt and validate signatures.
4) No-egress validation: perform network scan confirming kms-agent requires only the specified VPC endpoints and does not initiate other outbound connections.

Operator/ceremony notes:
- KEK rotation is expected to be an operator-driven event. We recommend quarterly KEK rotation for regulated healthcare customers; DEKs can rotate more frequently (30-day or per-major-release).
- For emergencies we include an "escrow recovery" path: the agent can export an emergency sealed-unlock package encrypted to multiple custodian public keys (split custodian approval required). This is part of the runbook.

Open items for your InfoSec:
- Which endpoint do you prefer for escrow ingest? (S3 bucket ARN we can PUT to, or SFTP host?)
- Do you want the escrow package schema to include plaintext metadata fields for auditors or fully opaque manifest with hashes?

If you share a preferred time we can schedule the 1-hour technical validation. I'll bring a short checklist and the draft escrow artifact for a walk-through.

Laura Bennett
Head of Security Integrations, Redwood Inference
